identity.title: Millimetre and sub-millimetre spectroscopy of doubly deuterated acetaldehyde (CHD<SUB>2</SUB>CHO) and first detection towards IRAS 16293-2422

paper_type_evidence.quote: Using this catalogue we were able to detect for the first time towards the low-mass protostellar system IRAS 16293-2422 utilizing data from the ALMA Protostellar Interferometric Line Survey.

Based on the new spectroscopic measurements, we searched for CHD$_{2}$CHO towards the B component of the protostellar system IRAS 16293–2422 in data from the ALMA Protostellar Interferometric Line Survey, PILS (cite: jorgensen:16).

question.value: Can doubly deuterated acetaldehyde (CHD2CHO) be detected in the interstellar medium towards IRAS 16293-2422 using a new laboratory spectroscopic catalogue, and what are its column density and D2/D ratio?

evidence.quote: A spectroscopic catalogue for astrophysical purposes is built for doubly deuterated acetaldehyde (CHD$_{2}$CHO) from measurements in the laboratory. With this accurate catalogue we aim to search and detect this species in the interstellar medium and retrieve its column density and abundance.

findings_qualitative.value: First detection of doubly deuterated acetaldehyde (CHD2CHO) in the interstellar medium towards IRAS 16293-2422 B

evidence.quote: Using this catalogue we were able to detect for the first time towards the low-mass protostellar system IRAS 16293-2422 utilizing data from the ALMA Protostellar Interferometric Line Survey.

findings_qualitative.value: The D2/D ratio (~20%) of acetaldehyde matches those of methyl formate, dimethylether, and methanol towards IRAS 16293-2422, pointing to a common formation environment (likely the pre-stellar core phase) with enhanced deuterium fractionation

evidence.quote: The resulting D$_{2}$/D ratio of $\sim$ 20% is found to be coincident with D$_{2}$/D ratios derived for other complex organic molecules towards IRAS 16293-2422, pointing at a common formation environment with enhanced deuterium fractionation.

The similar doubly to singly deuterated column density ratios for acetaldehyde, methyl formate, dimethylether and methanol presented in Section 3 suggest doubly deuterated acetaldehyde shares a common origin and was formed in an environment resembling the physical conditions with which doubly deuterated methyl formate, dimethylether and methanol were formed. The pre-stellar core phase is a good candidate

findings_qualitative.value: Doubly deuterated acetaldehyde is unlikely to be directly detectable towards pre-stellar cores due to low predicted 3 mm line brightness (0.5 mK)

evidence.quote: Based on our predictions it will be unlikely to detect the doubly deuterated acetaldehyde towards pre-stellar cores, and this is possibly true also for other COMs.

claims.hypothesis: Extending laboratory submillimetre spectroscopy of CHD2CHO to higher J and K_a transitions enables its first interstellar detection towards IRAS 16293-2422 B.
claims.experiment: Measured rotational transitions of CHD2CHO from 82.5 to 450 GHz in the laboratory, fitted 853 transitions with an IAM Hamiltonian to build a line catalogue up to J=28, and fitted LTE synthetic spectra to ALMA Band 7 PILS observations towards IRAS 16293-2422 B.
claims.result: Identified multiple clean, unblended transitions among 68 transitions predicted brighter than 40 mJy beam^-1 km s^-1, deriving a column density of 1.3 x 10^15 cm^-2 (uncertainty 10-20%) at T_rot = 125 K.
claims.finding: CHD2CHO is detected for the first time in the interstellar medium towards IRAS 16293-2422 B.

evidence.quote: A line position analysis is carried out allowing us to reproduce 853 transition frequencies with a weighted root mean square standard deviation of 1.7, varying 40 spectroscopic constants. A spectroscopic catalogue for astrophysical purposes is built from the analysis results. Using this catalogue we were able to detect for the first time towards the low-mass protostellar system IRAS 16293-2422 utilizing data from the ALMA Protostellar Interferometric Line Survey.
Several clean and unblended transitions are seen providing a good constraint on the CHD$_2$CHO column density of 1.3$\times 10^{15}$ cm$^{-2}$ with an uncertainty of 10-20%

claims.hypothesis: Doubly deuterated acetaldehyde shares a common formation environment with other complex organic molecules towards IRAS 16293-2422.
claims.experiment: Compared the derived CHD2CHO column density to the CH2DCHO column density from literature to obtain the D2/D ratio, and compared it with D2/D ratios of methyl formate, dimethylether, and methanol towards IRAS 16293-2422.
claims.result: The CHD2CHO/CH2DCHO ratio is ~20%, which is close to methyl formate (22%), dimethylether (15-20%), and methanol (25%), and 4–5 times higher than the singly-to-non-deuterated ratios.
claims.finding: Doubly deuterated acetaldehyde shares a common origin and formation environment with enhanced deuterium fractionation (likely the pre-stellar core phase) as other complex organic molecules.

evidence.quote: The ratio between the singly and doubly deuterated variants of 20% is very close to those for methyl formate (CHD$_2$OCHO/CH$_2$DOCHO) of 22% (cite: manigand:19), dimethylether (CH$_3$OCHD$_2$/CH$_2$OCH$_2$D) of 15-20% (cite: richard:21) and methanol (CHD$_{2}$OH/CH$_{2}$DOH) of 25% (cite: drozdovskaya:22) – in all cases significantly above the ratios for the singly-deuterated to non-deuterated isotopologues (cite: jorgensen:18) by factors of 4–5.

The similar doubly to singly deuterated column density ratios for acetaldehyde, methyl formate, dimethylether and methanol presented in Section 3 suggest doubly deuterated acetaldehyde shares a common origin and was formed in an environment resembling the physical conditions with which doubly deuterated methyl formate, dimethylether and methanol were formed.

claims.hypothesis: Doubly deuterated acetaldehyde can be detected directly in pre-stellar cores in the 3 mm band.
claims.experiment: Estimated the 3 mm line brightness of the most intense transitions of CH2DCHO and CHD2CHO using the average CH3CHO column density in starless cores (2 x 10^12 cm^-2) and the D/H and D2/H ratios from IRAS 16293-2422.
claims.result: Predicted line brightnesses are 4.3 mK for CH2DCHO and 0.5 mK for CHD2CHO.
claims.finding: It will be unlikely to detect doubly deuterated acetaldehyde towards pre-stellar cores.

evidence.quote: We estimate the line brightness of the most intense lines of the singly and doubly deuterated acetaldehyde in the 3 mm band towards pre-stellar cores to be 4.3 mK and 0.5 mK, respectively.
Based on our predictions it will be unlikely to detect the doubly deuterated acetaldehyde towards pre-stellar cores, and this is possibly true also for other COMs.

why_this_data.value: The ALMA PILS survey offers high sensitivity, high spatial resolution zooming into the warm gas around protostars, and relatively narrow lines towards IRAS 16293-2422 B, enabling unambiguous identification of deuterated COMs; the 0.5'' offset position limits line and continuum opacity.

evidence.quote: The high spatial-resolution of the interferometre allowed zooming-in into the warm gas around protostars where these molecules appear.
The high sensitivity of the PILS data and relatively narrow lines towards one component of IRAS 16293–2422 have enabled the detections of a number of species for the first time in the ISM
For our search we analysed the position offset by one beam (0.5$''$) from the B component of IRAS 16293–2422, where line and continuum opacity is limited.

why_this_method.value: High-barrier internal axis method (IAM) accounts for the internal rotation of an asymmetrical partially deuterated methyl group where symmetrical rotor models fail; LTE synthetic spectrum fitting is justified by the high gas densities in the warm protostellar region.

evidence.quote: These models cannot be used for molecules displaying internal rotation of a partially deuterated or methyl group. Alternate models were designed for such molecules

We adopted a similar approach to previous works by fitting synthetic spectra for CHD$_{2}$CHO calculated under the assumption that its excitation is characterised by local thermodynamical equilibrium (LTE), which is reasonable at the densities of the warm gas where these species are present (cite: jorgensen:16).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Symmetrical methyl group internal rotation models were rejected because they cannot be applied to molecules with a partially deuterated asymmetrical methyl group.

evidence.quote: The efforts to characterise the internal rotation of symmetrical methyl groups is still under study (cite: ilyushin:20; kleiner:20; xu:21). These models cannot be used for molecules displaying internal rotation of a partially deuterated or methyl group.

limitations_admitted.value: The energy difference E_d between the In and Out configurations and the parameters describing the 1 -> 3 tunneling path could not be retrieved from the spectroscopic fit because no couplings/transitions between the In and Out configurations were observed.

evidence.quote: No unaccountably large residuals, which could have been attributed to couplings between the In and Out configurations, were found. As a result, unlike in the monodeuterated species , the value of $E_d$ and of the parameters describing the $1\rightarrow3$ tunneling parameter could not be retrieved.

limitations_admitted.value: Large J and K_a a-type transitions show residuals larger than the 50 kHz experimental uncertainty, possibly due to unaccounted effects of the 1 -> 3 tunneling motion.

evidence.quote: $a$-type lines characterised by large $J$- and $K_a$-value tend to display residuals larger than this value and this may be due to the unaccounted for effects of the 1 $\rightarrow$ 3 tunneling motion.

limitations_admitted.value: A few lines in the astrophysical spectrum are under- or over-produced by the LTE model due to blending with brighter species or absorption from optically thick emission.

evidence.quote: The few lines that are either under- or over-produced with the synthetic spectra are due to blends with brighter lines of more prominent species (e.g the two lines seen at 330.71 GHz with an upper energy level of 202 K that are blended with glycolaldehyde) or absorption due to optically thick emission (e.g. the transition at 347.86 GHz falling close to a transition of formic acid).

referee_caveats_inferred: The rotational temperature (T_rot = 125 K), line width (1 km s^-1), and velocity offset (2.6 km s^-1) were fixed rather than fitted simultaneously with column density, which could affect the derived column density if excitation temperature differs from the main/singly-deuterated isotopologues.

The energy difference E_d between the In and Out conformers was not experimentally determined and relies on a B3LYP/6-31G(d) scaling of the monodeuterated species, introducing a small systematic uncertainty in the relative population of the In and Out states.

missing_for_reproduction: Exact sky coordinates of the 0.5'' offset position towards IRAS 16293-2422 B (requires looking up Jørgensen et al. 2016/2018)

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~1–50 GB for the reduced ALMA PILS spectral cubes (or a few MB for the extracted 1D spectrum at the 0.5'' offset position) plus a few MB for the CDS/CDMS spectroscopic tables
reproducibility.score_reason: The new spectroscopic catalogue is published at CDS/CDMS, the ALMA PILS data are public, and the fixed LTE parameters (T_rot = 125 K, FWHM = 1 km s^-1, v_LSR = 2.6 km s^-1) and 68 transitions are explicitly listed. However, exact extraction coordinates, source size/continuum treatment in LTE, and the specific radiative transfer fitting software are deferred to earlier PILS papers.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The ALMA PILS dataset (2013.1.00278.S) and the CDMS/CDS spectroscopic catalogue for CHD2CHO are publicly available, and the main astrophysical result is a numeric column density (1.3e15 cm^-2) and D2/D ratio (20%) derived with clearly stated LTE parameters.
